priorStories.headline: Judge halts FCC’s early ABC license reviews
priorStories.body:
A federal judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from continuing early license-renewal proceedings against eight ABC-owned television stations while litigation proceeds.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan found ABC likely to succeed on its claim that the proceedings retaliated against protected speech. The preliminary injunction pauses the reviews; it is not a final ruling on that claim. The court also denied the government’s motion to dismiss the lawsuit.

The FCC disputed the decision and said it expected to prevail.

sources.name: US District Court for the District of Columbia via The Desk

priorStories.headline: US inflation gauge records 3.8% annual rise
priorStories.body:
Consumer prices measured by the personal consumption expenditures index rose 3.8% in the year through October and 0.3% from September, the Bureau of Economic Analysis reported November 25. Excluding food and energy, prices increased 3.3% annually and 0.3% for the month.

Personal income rose 0.7% in October. Consumer spending increased 0.3% before accounting for inflation, but was essentially unchanged after adjusting for higher prices. The personal saving rate was 4.1%.

candidates.summary: Ahead of the EU summit in Brussels on November 26, European Council President António Costa said he sought to bring member states closer to agreement on the bloc’s next long-term budget. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said the Netherlands was not ready to accept the proposals on the table and called for a smaller, modernised budget. These were opening negotiating positions, not an agreed budget.
candidates.title: EU budget talks open with Dutch objections to proposals

candidates.summary: Bangchak said it shut all production units at its Phra Khanong refinery in Bangkok after a fire on November 26. The company said the fire began around 2:45 p.m. local time and was extinguished about 30 minutes later. Nine personnel were injured, two of whom subsequently returned home. A preliminary investigation placed the incident at the hydrocracking unit; the cause remained under investigation.
candidates.title: Bangchak shuts Bangkok refinery after fire injures nine

candidates.summary: Egyptian authorities announced on November 26 that they had detained a car driver suspected of causing the previous evening's fuel-tanker crash and fire on the Ring Road in Greater Cairo. Prosecutors said the driver told investigators his car struck the tanker while he was speeding between lanes; responsibility remained under investigation. Authorities reported at least 31 deaths and 26 injuries from the November 25 fire, which burned 27 vehicles.
candidates.title: Egypt announces detention in investigation of deadly Cairo tanker fire

candidates.summary: British Columbia's emergency information service reported at 8 a.m. local time on November 26 that Courtenay had upgraded an evacuation alert to an evacuation order for the Maple Pool/Headquarters Road area. Officials said floodwaters threatened life and safety and directed affected residents to leave immediately. A reception centre was available at Lower Native Sons Hall in Courtenay.
candidates.title: Flooding prompts evacuation order for part of Courtenay

candidates.summary: Government data reported on November 26 put confirmed Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo at 12,021 and deaths at 5,904. Reuters reported that the outbreak, declared in May in Ituri province, had spread to eight provinces. Conflict, delayed detection and strained health services continued to hamper containment. These are cumulative outbreak totals, not infections or deaths occurring on November 26 alone.
candidates.title: Congo reports more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases

candidates.summary: After November 26 EU budget talks in Brussels, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said leaders had moved toward reducing the proposed size of the next long-term budget but had not reached agreement. He said they would not reconvene on November 27 and would seek a deal at the December summit. Earlier, Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten had rejected the proposals on the table. Merz also said contributions to Ukraine aid remained under discussion that evening.
candidates.title: EU budget talks bring movement toward smaller proposal, Merz says

candidates.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military authorities announced on November 26 that presidential and legislative elections previously scheduled for December would be postponed until November 2028. A decree by transitional president Horta Inta-a cited insufficient technical, material and financial conditions for credible elections. The postponement extends the transition promised after the November 2025 coup by roughly two years.
candidates.title: Guinea-Bissau military authorities postpone elections until 2028

candidates.summary: European Council President António Costa said on November 26 that euro-area member states had agreed to recommend Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next European Central Bank president, alongside Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier for its executive board. Costa described the agreement as paving the way for formal appointments in December; the recommendation was not itself the final appointment.
candidates.title: Euro-area states recommend Hernández de Cos for ECB presidency

candidates.summary: Binance announced on November 26 that recovery work following its October security incident was complete and that the associated withdrawal suspension had been lifted. The company said withdrawals on a small number of networks remained temporarily paused for maintenance or planned upgrades, separately from the incident recovery.
candidates.title: Binance says post-incident withdrawal suspension has ended

candidates.summary: A Thanksgiving storm brought strong winds, coastal flooding and widespread electricity outages to the U.S. East Coast on November 26. Reuters reported that more than 836,000 utility customers nationwide lacked power at 4:06 p.m. Eastern, including more than 174,000 in Virginia, 172,000 in Maryland and almost 170,000 in Pennsylvania, citing PowerOutage.us. FlightAware recorded 417 U.S.-related flight cancellations and about 1,800 delays by Thursday afternoon. New York City Emergency Management reported a 56 mph gust at LaGuardia Airport.
candidates.title: Thanksgiving storm causes East Coast outages, flooding and flight disruption
candidates.geography: United States, particularly the East Coast

candidates.summary: Workers evacuated Venezuela's Amuay refinery during a fire on November 26, according to five PDVSA workers interviewed by Reuters. PDVSA confirmed that the fire was extinguished without injuries and said domestic fuel distribution was unaffected. One worker reported a temporary shutdown of the refinery's operating distillation unit; PDVSA did not confirm the unit's status or the cause of the fire.
candidates.title: Fire prompts evacuation at Venezuela's Amuay refinery

candidates.summary: Kenya's High Court ruled on November 26 that the process for establishing a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility at Laikipia Air Base violated constitutional requirements concerning public participation and access to information. KELIN, an interested party in the case, said the court suspended further work and ordered the government to disclose the U.S. agreement and related approvals within 45 days. The organization said it was awaiting the full written judgment.
candidates.title: Kenyan court suspends work on U.S.-backed Ebola facility

candidates.summary: A court in Mombasa convicted Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie on November 26 of organized criminal activity, radicalization, facilitating a terrorist act and possession of an article connected with a terrorism offense. Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty, and a lawyer said he would appeal after sentencing. These convictions were separate from the cruelty-to-children and assault convictions delivered on November 25.
candidates.title: Kenyan court convicts Paul Mackenzie on terrorism-related charges

candidates.summary: Swedish Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist said on November 26 that the party's board and parliamentary group recommended backing caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and joining a proposed four-party government. The recommendation still required the party governing council's support, and parliament had not yet voted on the premiership. The endorsement departed from the party's election campaign support for a centre-left government.
candidates.title: Swedish Centre leader recommends backing Kristersson government

candidates.summary: Kuwait's defense ministry said on November 26 that debris from intercepted drones killed two Italians and injured a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani. Kuwait attributed the drones to Iran. Italy's Foreign Ministry identified the Italians as civilian air-defense technicians working for a contractor on radar maintenance. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi denied Iranian responsibility in a call with his Italian counterpart. The attack location was not disclosed.
candidates.title: Kuwait reports two Italians killed by drone debris; Iran denies responsibility

candidates.summary: A Thanksgiving storm brought strong winds, coastal flooding and widespread electricity outages to the U.S. East Coast on November 26. Reuters, citing PowerOutage.us, reported more than 908,000 utility customers nationwide without electricity at 9:56 p.m. Eastern, down from 961,000 at 7:30 p.m. Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland and Virginia were among the hardest-hit states. FlightAware recorded 454 U.S.-related flight cancellations and 2,411 delays on Thursday.
candidates.title: Thanksgiving storm leaves more than 900,000 utility customers without power Thursday evening
candidates.geography: United States, particularly the East Coast

candidates.summary: New Zealand's Electoral Commission released the official November 7 election results at 2 p.m. November 27 local time, corresponding to 8 p.m. November 26 in New York. National won 40 seats, ACT 13 and New Zealand First 12, leaving the governing coalition with 65 of Parliament's 130 seats, one short of a majority. National lost two seats compared with preliminary results. Opportunity won seven seats. The official results remain subject to applications for judicial recounts.
candidates.title: New Zealand official election count leaves governing coalition one seat short of majority

candidates.summary: Australia announced counterterrorism financing sanctions against Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad on November 27 local time, during the November 26 evening in New York. Foreign Minister Penny Wong said authorities assessed that the two had used proxies to orchestrate 2024 arson attacks against a Sydney kosher restaurant and Melbourne's Adass Israel Synagogue on behalf of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Iran has denied responsibility for the attacks. The sanctions restrict the individuals' access to funds.
candidates.title: Australia sanctions two alleged organizers of Iranian-directed antisemitic arson attacks

candidates.summary: South Korea returned six rescued North Korean fishing crew members by sea after confirming their wishes, Seoul's Unification Ministry said. Their boat crossed the maritime border at 8:33 a.m. November 27 Korean time, corresponding to 6:33 p.m. November 26 in New York. A seventh crew member chose to remain in South Korea and receive protection. The vessel had been found drifting near Ulleung Island on November 3. Authorities said they coordinated notification of the return through the United Nations Command.
candidates.title: South Korea returns six rescued North Koreans while seventh chooses to stay

candidates.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency said on November 26 that it was working with Russia and Ukraine to arrange a local ceasefire for repairs to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant's external electricity connection. The plant was relying on emergency diesel generators after losing its remaining external power line on November 25, reportedly because of military activity. The agency described this as the plant's 28th loss of offsite power during the conflict. A ceasefire had not been announced as agreed.
candidates.title: IAEA seeks local ceasefire to repair Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant power connection
